stories.title: Indonesian police name 72 suspects in crackdown on land burning in Kalimantan
stories.summary: Indonesian police have named 72 suspects in deliberate land burning linked to clearing land for oil palm plantations in Kalimantan and Sumatra. President Prabowo ordered rapid disaster response, deploying army battalions and firefighting equipment to control spreading fires, especially in Kalimantan's peatlands. Authorities are investigating companies’ involvement, with possible permit revocations if found guilty, while the President plans to visit quake-hit East Nusa Tenggara soon. The Indonesian police have named 72 suspects in their crackdown on deliberate land burning after President Prabowo Subianto ordered over the weekend a rapid response to disasters ravaging parts of the country, including efforts to contain the land fires in Kalimantan and Sumatra. The National Police’s Criminal Investigation Department (Bareskrim) on Aug 23 said police investigations across five provinces in Kalimantan and four in Sumatra found evidence suggesting that fires detected through satellite-monitored hot spots had been deliberately set by the suspects.

stories.title: FTC proposes guidelines to boost transparency at prepaid installment firms
stories.summary: South Korea's fair trade watchdog said Monday it issued an administrative notice of proposed revisions to consumer protection guidelines for prepaid installment transactions, aimed at strengthening transparency in operators' management of customers' advance payments. The Fair Trade Commission (FTC) said the proposed revisions would require operators to establish internal guidelines for managing advance payments and draw up a management plan for each fiscal year. In South Korea, funeral or travel service providers commonly use prepaid installment contracts, under which customers make a series of advance payments for services to be provided at a later date. Under the proposed guidelines, operators would be required to balance stability, liquidity and profitability when managing advance payments to ensure sufficient funds remain available to provide contracted services and pay cancellation refunds. They would also be required to conduct thorough reviews before investing in high-risk assets, including derivatives. Operators holding 100 billion won (US$72.1 million) or more in advance payments would be required to establish a management review committee.
